task_reconstruction.official_task: Find bottlenecks at an airport checkpoint and modifications that raise throughput and cut variance.

section_map.summary: Summary names three bottlenecks and two gains.
NetLogo agent model with four queues.
Recommendations as a short action list.

contributions.summary: A four-digit code for checkpoint configurations.
Modifications compared as ratios against one baseline.

dependency_graph.handoff: the per-queue waits the bottleneck comparison reads
the baseline throughput each modification is scored against

assumptions.summary: Solo travel, unlimited queues, one arrival per second.
Two screening lines share one metal detector and one body scanner.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Shapiro-Wilk at 0.01 keeps two normal distributions.
Generation probability 0.19 counted over nine minutes.

models.summary: Agent simulation, one hour, four queues.
Bottleneck is the queue with the largest mean wait.

verification.summary: At least three runs per configuration, then averaged.
Normality checked by test and by Q-Q plot.

results_trace.summary: Wait of 20.51 and 232.39 seconds at probabilities 0.09 and 0.18.
Standard deviation of 1409.13 seconds at probability 0.72.
Two PreCheck officers nearly double throughput; a third adds little.
Extra metal detector multiplies throughput by 1.22 and 1.43.

writing_logic.summary: Each measure defined before it is used.
Changes reported as ratios, baseline kept visible.
Strengths and weaknesses alternate, one sentence each.

language_observations.summary: Bottlenecks named, then their share of variance.
A layout encoded as a four-digit code.
A negative effect reported as smaller than expected.

visualization_observations.summary: Table 4 splits wait by queue and by passenger type.
Table 9 gives throughput ratios across five traffic levels.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: Ratio tables let a judge check each claimed gain.

independent_extensions.summary: Reconcile the summary's 30 minute standard deviation with the 1409.13 seconds in table 5.

candidate_rule_impacts.impact: Two configurations, one per traffic band.
Passengers routed to the shortest lane.
Times tested for normality before use.
Officer count chosen where the gain flattens.
Summary and table disagree on the peak spread.
Prose percentages disagree with the ratio table.
Cutting and slow walking modeled as behaviors.

unresolved_questions: Summary says standard deviation tops 30 minutes; table 5 prints 1409.13 seconds. Both kept.
Prose claims gains of 28 to 82 percent; table 9 prints 1.22 and 1.43. Both kept.
Page 1 has no text layer. Its summary was read from the rendered page.
